title: Sunday · the Rain, 2005
logline: Eighth January. The first Rain that the watercolor gets right. Three tiers. Nothing else.

panels.composition: Tier 1: the beach in rain. The wash controlled now — rain as a gray veil, the surf a white line, the sand a mirror.

image.prompt: a Pacific Northwest beach in January rain in controlled watercolor: rain as a gray veil, the surf a white line, wet sand mirroring a white sky, ink line beneath, no figures

panels.name: Veil

panels.composition: Tier 2: the spruce grove. Green and black kept separate this time. A man and a dog, small, at its foot.

image.prompt: a dark spruce grove in watercolor with the greens and blacks kept clean, a small man and a small dog at its foot in rain, no words

panels.name: Grove

panels.composition: Tier 3: the two of them from behind, walking home up the beach, the rain thinning — the same three tiers as January 2004, done right.

image.prompt: a man and a dog from behind walking up a rainy beach as the rain thins, controlled gray and sea-green watercolor, no words
image.notes: A deliberate redo of the January 2004 Sunday. Same three tiers; the reader compares.

panels.name: Home

art.palette: limited, muddy; Sundays in watercolor, improving

notes: The 2004 Rain redone a year later, competent. The book runs them a hundred pages apart.
